core.title: Bind each journey spec to exactly one train or journey
core.given: A journey spec: an e2e test spec (recognised by the stack's e2e test name pattern), or any test file whose binding position — the position, given by the stack's binding syntax, where binding lines and URN reference markers are declared — carries a journey marker (a train or journey binding marker, or a train or journey URN reference).
core.when: the spec is present in the scanned tree (new or existing, whether or not its binding was touched)
core.then: its binding declaration carries exactly one binding — to one train or to one journey — whose id matches the planning side's identity grammar.
prefer: Add the binding in the stack's binding position, using the stack's binding syntax, binding the spec to the one train or journey it exercises.
avoid: A journey spec with no binding.
An id the planning side would reject.
Renaming a spec so it no longer matches the e2e test name pattern to escape the check — journey markers still bring it in scope.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
Unit and acceptance tests carrying none of the journey markers are out of scope.
core.why: The binding is how a journey-level (e2e) test is traced to the plan it exercises; a spec with no binding, two bindings, or an id the planning side would reject cannot be traced.
evidence: The stack's convention check reports zero findings for every journey spec: exactly one binding, its id matching the planning side's identity grammar.
A reviewer can read the spec's binding position and see a single binding to one train or journey.
verification: Scope: every e2e test spec (by the stack's e2e test name pattern), plus any test file whose binding position carries a journey marker (a binding marker or a URN reference marker) — a misnamed spec is still judged. Both binding markers and reference markers are read at the same position, the one given by the stack's binding syntax.
A journey URN appearing only in a string (not in the binding position) does not make a file a journey spec.
Count the bindings (train and journey) in the spec's binding position; exactly one is required. Zero or more than one is a finding.
Each binding's id is validated against the planning side's identity grammar (the stack's train and journey id shapes).

Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact classification of which paths count as vendored or generated is owned by this rule's check, in addition to the stack's stack-wide never-scanned list.
Applies to every in-scope journey spec in the scanned tree, not only newly added or edited ones.

values: journey marker in the binding position: train or journey binding marker, or train/journey URN reference

fires: An e2e test spec (new or already existing, its binding touched or not) has no train or journey binding.
A test file that does not match the e2e test name pattern carries a train or journey URN reference in its binding position but no binding.
A journey spec carries both a train and a journey binding, or more than one binding to the same kind.
A journey spec's binding id does not match the planning side's identity grammar (for example a train id missing a part).
doesNotFire: A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string and has no journey marker in its binding position.
Unit or acceptance tests carrying none of the journey markers.
Files in the stack's vendored and generated (never-scanned) trees.

neutralityNotes: All concrete syntax is pushed into the profile: the e2e name pattern (suffix.e2e_test), the train/journey id shapes (urn.train, urn.journey), and the binding and reference marker syntaxes (urn.binding.train/journey, and the proposed urn.reference.train/journey). The binding and reference values now carry the placement idiom — Bun's header comment block — so the core's 'binding position' is fully defined by the profile for any stack (another stack's realization would supply its own position, e.g. a decorator, through the same keys); the core does not depend on the Bun-only scanner description for layout. Reference markers are read at the same position as bindings, stated in the core given/verification and in the profile values. The vendored/generated exclusion is kept as a neutral never-scan clause whose exact classification is owned by this rule's check (verification[4]), per the vocabulary's rule that roots.excluded is one stack-wide list and a checker's own classification lives in the rule's verification; Bun's four tree names are bunOnly. The Playwright qualifier and the detector id (htmx_e2e_detector) are realization details kept as bunOnly. 'The planner's identity grammar' is expressed through urn.train/urn.journey; any stricter planner-side grammar remains on the plan side and is not further specified by either the core or the Bun rule.
